answer: Each identity claims one bridge span and fits a lotus gauge for test-load deflection. A span auditor recomputes expected deflection from the span table and load; an out-of-tolerance reading burns the 60-credit bond held in a vault. The first span pays 32 credits, each earlier span adds 5, so the k-th fake locks 60 plus 32+5(k-1), the 1000th pays 5087, and 1000 fakes risk 2,589,500. Honest agents pay 32 once and reclaim the bond on a match. A rented-gauge ring fails because a lotus gauge serial binds to one span and load, so reuse mismatches stiffness and burns every bond.
